title: Flint-interactive: A language for creating interactive data visualizations - Microsoft Research
gist: Microsoft Research introduced Flint-interactive, a high-level language on top of the Flint visualization compiler that lets AI agents and developers specify chart interactions as mappings from semantic events to update operators, while the compiler handles hit testing and rendering. It targets the high token cost and unreliability of agents hand-coding interactive charts, and is usable in chat via Flint-MCP and MCP Apps or in apps via Flint Interactive Canvas.

themes.theme: Why agents struggle with interactive charts

insights.claim: Microsoft Research says even capable frontier-model agents struggle to generate interactive data visualizations because they rarely succeed in one turn, so repeated reasoning, coding and debugging rounds drive up token cost and time, and fixes often introduce broken layouts or interactions.
insights.speaker: Brenda Potts
insights.so_what: Domain-specific languages that cut agent retry loops are one lever for lowering inference cost in agentic analytics products.
insights.quote: Agents rarely produce a fully satisfactory interactive visualization in one turn.

insights.claim: Microsoft Research attributes the difficulty of agent-built interactive visualizations to the lack of an expressive yet high-level language for specifying visual interactions, since built-in interactions in visualization libraries are not expressive enough for bespoke charts.
insights.speaker: Brenda Potts
insights.so_what: Points to an abstraction-layer gap in BI tooling that agent-native visualization languages aim to fill.
insights.locator: These challenges help explain why consistently

insights.claim: Flint-interactive separates visual logic, which the Flint compiler resolves by turning raw clicks, drags and key presses into semantic events and update operators into rendered changes, from interaction logic, which the user or agent specifies by mapping semantic events to operators such as set style, set annotation or set viewport.
insights.speaker: Brenda Potts
insights.so_what: Moving complexity into a compiler makes agent output more reliable and cheaper, a pattern likely to spread across agent tooling.
insights.quote: This shifts the heavy burden of resolving complex dependencies between interaction and visual logic to the compiler

insights.claim: Because Flint-interactive's event generation and visual updates are compositional, charts can be linked to tables, text, other charts and widgets, so an action in one view can update another view or application state in dashboards and data stories.
insights.speaker: Brenda Potts
insights.so_what: Cross-view interactivity generated by agents could compete with traditional BI dashboards built by hand.

insights.claim: Flint-interactive can be used directly in chat or canvas environments through Flint-MCP and MCP Apps, where the agent generates an interaction_spec alongside the Flint chart spec, renders the interactive chart in the conversation and lets the user's selections pass context to follow-up turns.
insights.speaker: Brenda Potts
insights.so_what: Shows MCP becoming the channel for shipping rich UI components into agent chat interfaces.

insights.claim: Developers can embed Flint Interactive Canvas in dashboards or data stories, handle its emitted semantic events to filter tables or update state, send update operators back to it, and build bespoke interactions via a programming API that maps events to custom update sequences.
insights.speaker: Brenda Potts
insights.so_what: An open developer surface could make Flint a building block for third-party analytics apps.
insights.locator: 2. Build an interactive app with Flint

insights.claim: The Flint-interactive authors include Microsoft Research's Chenglong Wang, Michel Galley, Chris Quirk and Technical Fellow Jianfeng Gao, UCLA PhD student Yuwei Xiao, and Power BI senior data visualization engineer Alper Sarikaya.
insights.speaker: Brenda Potts
insights.so_what: Power BI involvement suggests a possible path for this research into Microsoft's commercial BI product.
